title: Disconnect-recovery microflow set for SDK streaming + token refresh visuals
creator: Mina Alvarez
description: Deliver a focused asset pack and UX spec showing how the SDK onboarding guides users through transient network failures, token refresh, and API-key rotation while streaming and invoking tools. This ticket covers static screenshots, annotated microflow diagrams, 3 lightweight GIF sequences for the docs site, and accessible alt-text copy for each asset. Goals: 1) reduce support questions related to 'stream disconnects' and 'invalid token mid-stream', 2) show clear callouts for automatic retry/backoff and token refetch, and 3) provide copy variants for self-serve and enterprise docs. Deliverables: - 8x high-res screenshots (desktop + narrow mobile) showing: initial connection, interrupted stream with inline retry CTA, background token refresh with subtle progress HUD, successful reconnection with resumed KV cache, and key-rotation confirmation modal. - 3x GIFs (10s max) demonstrating: automatic reconnect sequence, manual key-swap flow in Console, and streaming with ephemeral token refresh mid-session. - 1x annotated microflow SVG for docs (lightweight, accessible labels) describing sequence: connect -> detect 401/timeout -> token refresh -> retry -> success/fallback. - Copy + alt-text for each asset and a short help-center blurb (120–220 chars) for support. Constraints: keep visuals consistent with existing SDK palette, keep overlays low-contrast-friendly, avoid implying automatic state-full model restarts (we only show token retry and prefix cache resume). Link to PRD: https://redwood.atlassian.com/confluence/onboarding/recover-streams (placeholder). Figma frames: https://www.figma.com/file/abcdef/stream-recovery-onboard (placeholder). GitHub demo PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/412 (placeholder). Acceptance criteria (must pass to move to Done): - Assets uploaded to the docs/assets/stream-recovery/ directory in required sizes. - Every screenshot has written alt-text and a short support blurb. - GIFs preview correctly in Chrome and Safari and are under 2MB each. - Design review signoff from PM (Riley Park) and Eng reviewer (Priya Rao). - Implementation notes for dev (CSS overlays, reduced-motion variants) included in comments.
